lines: There you are. Late again, but I will forgive it. I was late to my own first lesson, and my teacher never let me forget it.
You have read the three Colours and the Weave until the pages wore thin. Today we stop reading. Today you cast.
Ask me what you like first. A wizard who does not ask questions is only a person with dangerous hands.

title: The mentor's three skill questions on a fresh apprentice

lines: You know your three colours. Try your hand against my Ward when you are ready.
ask_wards.text:
Skebok Hardfist leans on the staff and considers you for a moment.
Nobody asks that. Good. Three is the smallest number that can hide a pattern and still be a pattern. The old masters wove their Wards so that a Ward remembers the hand that wrote it. Mine remembers me. Yours will remember you.

lines: You know your three colours. Try your hand against my Ward when you are ready.

title: The mentor's log errand
claim: ‘Is there anything you need?’ then the keeper's log choice then the thanks.

observed.mentor_asks: Since you ask: a log for the brazier. The store has them; the keeper will give you one if you ask kindly, and will not if you do not. I am old and I feel the cold, and that is the whole of the errand.
keeper_choices: What's the matter with the warehouse?
Those are not rats. They are machines. Look at the legs.
My teacher needs a log for the brazier. Could the store spare one?
observed.keeper_reply: For Skebok Hardfist? Take one. Take it from the dry stack, not the green. And tell them the account is open; they never let it close.
mentor_thanks: You brought the log. Dry, from the good stack; the keeper likes you, then, which is rarer than you think.
The brazier will burn tonight. Thank you. Now, what else?

title: The stranger's confrontation, page by page
claim: Ten pages: narration, mentor and stranger argue, the mentor is killed on page 7, the stranger speaks to you (page 10), a final page offers challenge or silence.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Skebok Hardfist has stopped what they were doing. The staff that has leaned in the corner of every lesson is in their hand.

pages.speaker: Skebok Hardfist
pages.text: Istthea Saltrunner. I had hoped never to see this day. You have grown thin.

pages.speaker: Istthea Saltrunner
pages.text: Thin. Yes. Ten winters of doing what you would not teach me to do. I walked through the blight at Harrowmere while you taught children to light candles. They begged for anyone with power to command the sickness, the lords, anything. Nobody was permitted to. I learned what that costs.

pages.speaker: Skebok Hardfist
pages.text: And you decided that the answer was to be the one permitted. Power is not a licence, Istthea Saltrunner. It is what we owe the ones who cannot do what we can.

pages.speaker: Istthea Saltrunner
pages.text: A comforting thing to say with a roof over your head. I came to ask you once more to stand with me. The Weave answers to the strongest. The world should too.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Istthea Saltrunner lifts one hand. The light under his cloak opens like a door. Skebok Hardfist raises a Ward, a good one, three-fold and old, and it shatters like thin ice.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: Skebok Hardfist falls. The staff rolls across the dirt and lies still. All around the square, people stop and stare.

pages.speaker: narrator
pages.text: He turns. For the first time he sees you.

pages.speaker: Istthea Saltrunner
pages.text: The apprentice. A child with a borrowed staff. Your teacher was the best of them, and it took me less than a breath.
answers_open: He was weaker than you. That is simply how power works.
Nobody gave you the right to do this.
He kept his vows. You have broken every one of yours.
You have torn something out of this place that will not grow back.
He taught half this village their trade. What does your grievance pay for that?
He had a duty to this village. You had no claim on it at all.
pages.answer_text: Your voice shakes on the second word. He hears it.
pages.stranger_reply: "Brave. Brave is what the dead are told they were."

pages.speaker: Istthea Saltrunner
pages.text: I am not a butcher, and you are not enough: not for me, not yet for anything. Become more. There is a craft older than the schools, and I mean to teach the world what it is for. When you can bear to stand against me, come and find me.
answers_open: Then prove it. Ward against Ward, here, now.
pages.answer_text: You keep your hands where they are. He waits a moment longer than he needs to, then turns away.
pages.stranger_reply: "Wise. Or frightened. From here they look the same."

title: Belief replies to the stranger and how he takes them
claim: Seven replies, one per worldview; the stranger (main S, second C) agrees with S, is neutral to A, G and C, and disagrees with M, R and D. ‘C’ needs the mentor's old-craft secret.

S.reply: "At last, a student who has been listening. Weakness is not a crime, boy, but it is a verdict."

A.reply: "Rights are what the strong have left over. Hold on to yours, if you can."

R.reply: "Vows are what the weak swear to feel safe. Spare me the sermon."

D.reply: "Balance is what the powerless call their fear. Spare me the hill-talk."

G.reply: "A trade, a debt. Everything balances in the end."

M.reply: "A claim needs someone to enforce it. Look around you: who is enforcing his?"

C.reply: "If it is a play, it is the only one I can bear to stay in."

victory_pages.speaker: narrator

victory_pages.speaker: Istthea Saltrunner

victory_pages.speaker: narrator

victory_pages.speaker: narrator

title: The Trial's choice events, branch by branch
claim: Each choice event offers its choices, applies its consequences once, and remembers the run state.

statue_riddle.text:
A knight went first. She counted the steps from the door to this stone; she said it aloud so I would remember. Half as many again as the years I have stood here, and I have stood here a hundred.

How many steps did she count?

No. Listen better; the Trial will not ask twice.

He raps your knuckles with his staff, hard enough to numb the hand. You are hurt: one cast fewer in your next duel.

Beside him stands a knight in White Road armour, turned to stone mid-step. Serra went first. This is where first got her.

A hundred and fifty. She could count; it did not save her.

So I will tell you one thing for it. The lion-thing that guards the last door hates the light. Remember that when you weave against it.

throm_pit.text:
A pit cuts the corridor. Far below, water moves. The far edge is a long jump, or a rope's length, if someone holds the rope.

Throm: "I hold the rope, or you hold it for me. Or we jump it together, and laugh."
Throm: "Down you go, villager. I have held worse."

Throm: "...Throm. My name is Throm. Take the rope, then. Tightly."

You lower Throm by the rope. He looks very small, and then he waves you off the edge.

You take the wall alone. Halfway, the wall takes you. You land in the shallows, hard. You are hurt: one cast fewer in your next duel. Your torch hisses out in the water and goes to the bottom.

Throm: "Hah. Wait there; I am coming down the sensible way."

You jump together, land hard, and laugh until it hurts.

(It hurts. You are hurt: one cast fewer in your next duel.)
Throm: "Hah. An honest villain would have left. Come on."

You cross alone. Behind you, the rope goes still.

You will remember this.
The rope is tied off below. Throm went down first; the knots are his. Climb when you like.
The rope hangs slack into the dark. Nobody is holding it. You crossed alone, and you will remember this.
The rope is tied off below. Throm is down there somewhere, favouring one arm.

black_book.text: It tastes of ink and lightning. Your hands shake. You are poisoned: your next casts will come slower than you would like.
It burns cold. Where it touches, the skin knits a little, though there was nothing much to knit.
It burns cold. Where it touches, the skin knits a little, though there was nothing much to knit.
You stopper the vial and leave it. Some things stay unknown.

dwarf_meet.text: Dwarf: "Locked in, both of you. Only one continues; that is the procedure. The Trialmaster at your service: locked doors are my speciality."

Dwarf: "Through here. Mind the cobra."

Dwarf: "Two dice in the cup. When they land: the same as eight, less, or more?"

Dwarf: "Oh, we do this every Trial."

Something clicks. Throm sits down suddenly, holding his head. "We do it MY way," the Dwarf says. You are hurt: one cast fewer in your next duel.

Dwarf: "Two dice in the cup. When they land: the same as eight, less, or more?"

Dwarf: The cup lifts: 10. "Wrong. But you understood the question, which is the point."

Dwarf: "Last: the basket. Hold its gaze, or snatch it. Choose."

You hold its gaze until it looks away first. The Dwarf writes something down.

He unrolls a scrap of oiled hide: the lower Trial, in a hand that has drawn it many times. Three gems marked. A door marked that wants Emerald, Sapphire and Diamond. And a passage from this very room, west, that is not on anyone else's map.

Watching him weave the lock shut, you learn a fourth colour: Stone.

Dwarf: "The cobra is ready. He waits in the arena. Finish it." Throm is dragged in, and his eyes do not know you.

elf_rescue.text: The snake loosens. The elven woman breathes, barely. She is fading.

You hold her hand while she tells you: the final door wants gems, and one of them is a diamond. The real one is cold.

Dying elf: "Take the charm. Take the bread. ...Tell the trees I was brave."
You take the charm. Her voice follows you out: the final door wants gems, one is a diamond, and the real one is cold.
She is gone. The hollow smells of bread and dust.

false_eye.text: The east eye glitters. Bigger. Greener. The scratched warnings around the base were about this one.

It comes away in your hand, glass, flawed glass, and every bird on the idol turns its head at once.

The second guardian does not wait to be found. It finds you.
Nothing else moves. You are holding a piece of green glass in a room full of dead birds.
You leave it where it lies.
A socket, empty, and a room full of dead birds.

false_diamond.text:
You remember the elf: the real one is cold. This one has been lying under a lamp.

A diamond beside a fallen warrior, just lying there. Every instinct says trap.

You remember the elf: the real one is cold. This one has been lying under a lamp.

A diamond beside a fallen warrior, just lying there. Every instinct says trap.

The floor opens its eye. A blade you never see draws a line across your arm, and somewhere behind you an iron bolt shoots home.

You are hurt: one cast fewer in your next duel. The jewel is glass. The inner vault has locked itself; the Basket man's rope is now the only way in.
You leave it where it lies.

free_prisoner.text: Starved man: "...failed... they took my eyes... no, my boots..."

You cut his bonds. He presses something into your hand, bitter herbs, and babbles about the beast below.

Starved man: "Go. Stones. It loves... no. It HATES the green. Vine. Its eyes water."

(The Bloodbeast's Ward will not hold Vine.)
You leave him. The dark keeps him.

ivy_toll.text: Poison Ivy: "Tribute, sweetling. Something useful, or thorns."
Poison Ivy: "A torch? For me? ...Walk soft, sweetling. Walk soft."
The thorns come up all at once.

basket_ride.text: Basket man: "Rope's for staff and for people Ivy likes. You're neither, yet. Sort her out, or sort out the poor sod in the cell, and we'll talk."
Basket man: "Heard what you did. Right. The rope goes up to the vault's back room and comes down again; use the shaft at the south wall whenever you like. Don't tell the Dwarf."
Basket man: "Shaft's at the south wall. Up or down, same fare: none."

mirror_smash.text: Tall mirrors, silver-backed. Something moves in them a breath after you do.

Silver rain. The thing in the glass never finishes stepping out.

(The Mirror Demon is broken without a duel. Something bright lies in the frame.)
You leave the glass its dignity.
Silver dust, and a frame with nothing in it.

boulder_run.text: The tunnel exhales dust. Uphill, something heavy decides.
You run like the Trial is behind you. It is. The groove in the floor runs straight; you don't. The boulder agrees to miss.
You lay Stone across the groove and lean on it. The boulder arrives, argues, and loses. Behind it, the side tunnel is open and full of somebody's abandoned kit.
You lay Stone across the groove and lean on it. The boulder arrives, argues, and loses. Behind it, the side tunnel is open and full of somebody's abandoned kit.

You hold your ground. The ground holds. You don't.

You are hurt: one cast fewer in your next duel.
Dust settles in the groove. Whatever rolled has rolled.

trapped_chest.text: An iron-bound chest, lid a finger's width open. Gold glints inside. So does something else, at floor height.

You stand where the floor is unscratched and lift the lid with the butt of your staff. Blades whicker out across the place you are not standing.

The gold is real.

Teeth. The chest had teeth, and the marks on the floor had told you exactly where.

You are hurt: one cast fewer in your next duel. The gold is real, at least.
You leave the gold to whatever guards it.
The chest stands open, its blades spent. The gold is gone.

trog_ritual.text: Ritual elder: "The rite, stranger. Dance it, run it, or bleed it. The tribe does not mind which."
You dance badly and sincerely. The tribe approves of sincerity.
Bridges, drums, black water, and then, impossibly, quiet.
Their champion steps out of the drumming.
Ritual elder: "Danced. Witnessed. Go with wet feet, stranger."
The drums have stopped. The tribe keeps its distance.

igbut_door.text: Igbut: "Three gems, contestant. Emerald. Sapphire. Diamond. The door does the rest."
Igbut: "It waits. It is good at waiting."

Igbut: "The gnome counts on his fingers. Counts again."

Igbut: "Emerald. Sapphire. Diamond. THREE are required, contestant. The Trial does not bargain."
Igbut: "Three sockets. Three gems. Place them true, and mind the bite."

The sockets drink the gems. The door sighs open.

Igbut: "Ha! Walk through, Champion..."

A crossbow sings from the dark Sukumvit built. Igbut does not finish.

You walk past him into daylight, and Fang roars your name.

CHAMPION OF THE TRIAL

Igbut: "1 placed true, 2 displaced."

The door bites. You are hurt: one cast fewer in your next duel.

Igbut: "1 placed true, 2 displaced."

The third blast throws the gems out of your hands and across the floor. The sockets grind shut.

Igbut, from behind the plinth: "They reopen. They always reopen. Pick up your stones, contestant."

title: The mentor's pointer to the village quarrel
claim: ‘What should I do now?’ names the three villagers and where to find them.

observed.text:
Not a spell. Listen. Walk through the village, speak to the carriers, the foresters, the guards. A wizard who has never carried a log or stood a watch casts for people he does not understand.
There is a quarrel you might hear: Ragtor Blackshield the lumberjack and Kormund Thunderaxe the forester have stopped speaking. One wants every ripe tree down for the sawmill, the other wants the young ones left to grow. Hrunrik Longfist saw part of it. Ragtor Blackshield works at the lumberjack's hut, about 19 tiles west of you. Kormund Thunderaxe works at the forester's hut, about 22 tiles west of you. It is no emergency, and you need not help; but they are ordinary people with a real disagreement, and what you say will be remembered.

title: A wizard who was away while the stranger came and went

ann_journal_on_return: A fellow apprentice broke the stranger's Ward, and he withdrew from the village, alive.
